subjects.displayTitle: Receiving revelation: the Spirit and its expression
subjects.introduction: In the stench and chains of the Síyáh-Chál, Bahá’u’lláh felt something flow from the crown of His head over His breast like a torrent hurled from a mountain top, and His tongue recited what no one could bear to hear. Revelation is described from the inside here, as a voice above the head, a Maiden suspended in the air, a wind that will not let the leaf lie still. Alongside stands ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s explanation of what is received: the Holy Spirit is the outpouring grace and perfections of God, related to the Manifestation as rays to the sun, so that Jesus is the Christ precisely because those perfections shine in Him, and souls draw grace from that light rather than from a personality. Mark’s scene of the heavens opening and the Spirit descending like a dove at the Jordan [1] offers a Christian image to set beside these, each keeping its own claims. Bahá’u’lláh names revelation the gift on which every other gift depends, and the real test of having received it is the virtues it awakens. The inquiry leads onward to the Manifestation as mediator and as pen, to the Holy Spirit itself, and to the modes and manner of revelation.
subjects.arc: Begin with revelation amid confinement, explore the relation of Spirit and Manifestation, and follow symbolic expression toward its effects upon human life.

order.why: Open with the vivid account of revelation amid imprisonment.
shortened: During the days I lay in the prison of Tihran, though the galling weight of the chains and the stench-filled air allowed Me but little sleep, still in those infrequent moments of slumber I felt as if something flowed from the crown of My head over My breast, even as a mighty torrent that precipitateth itself upon the earth from the summit of a lofty mountain. Every limb of My body would, as a result, be set afire. At such moments My tongue recited what no man could bear to hear.

order.why: Hear the impulse to speak expressed through wind and a leaf.
shortened: Every time I hold my peace, and cease to extol Thy wondrous virtues, Thy Spirit impelleth me to cry out before all who are in Thy heaven and on Thy earth; and every time I am still, the breaths wafted from the right hand of Thy will and purpose pass over me, and stir me up, and I find myself to be as a leaf which lieth at the mercy of the winds of Thy decree, and is carried away whithersoever Thou dost permit or command it.

order.why: Consider utterance as dependence upon divine inspiration.
shortened: From my pen floweth only the summons which Thine own exalted pen hath voiced, and my tongue uttereth naught save what the Most Great Spirit hath itself proclaimed in the kingdom of Thine eternity. I am stirred by nothing else except the winds of Thy will, and breathe no word except the words which, by Thy leave and Thine inspiration, I am led to pronounce.

order.why: Follow inspiration into a summons to service.
shortened: Proclaim, then, that which the Most Great Spirit will inspire thee to utter in the service of the Cause of thy Lord, that thou mayest stir up the souls of all men and incline their hearts unto this most blessed and all-glorious Court.

order.why: Read revelation as the gift upon which other gifts depend.
shortened: That which is preeminent above all other gifts, is incorruptible in nature, and pertaineth to God Himself, is the gift of Divine Revelation. Every bounty conferred by the Creator upon man, be it material or spiritual, is subservient unto this.
He hath, indeed, partaken of this highest gift of God who hath recognized His Manifestation in this Day.

order.why: Introduce the image of grace radiating through Christ.
shortened: Question: What is meant by the Holy Spirit?

Answer: By the Holy Spirit is meant the outpouring grace of God and the effulgent rays that emanate from His Manifestation. Thus Christ was the focal centre of the rays of the Sun of Truth, and from this mighty centre--the reality of Christ--the grace of God shone upon the other mirrors which were the realities of the Apostles.

order.why: Distinguish the Manifestation and the perfections manifested.
shortened: Answer: The sanctified realities of the Manifestations of God have two spiritual stations: One is that of the state of divine manifestation, which can be compared to the orb of the sun, and the other is that of radiance and revelation, which may be likened to the divine light and perfections--the Holy Spirit. For the Holy Spirit is the manifold grace and perfections of God, and these divine perfections are even as the rays and heat of the sun.

If the perfections of God were not revealed and manifested in Jesus, He would not be Christ. He is a Manifestation of God precisely because the divine perfections are revealed in Him. The Prophets of God are Manifestations, and the divine perfections--that is, the Holy Spirit--are that which is manifested in Them.

order.why: Consider their inseparability through the sun and its light.
shortened: The third station is that of divine grace, the revelation of the beauty of the Ancient of Days and the effulgence of the lights of the ever-living and omnipotent Lord. The individual realities of the holy Manifestations cannot be separated from divine grace and revelation any more than the corporeal mass of the sun can be separated from its light.

order.why: Read the timeless station of the Word and Holy Spirit.
shortened: The third station is that of divine manifestation and heavenly splendour, which is the Word of God, the everlasting Grace, and the Holy Spirit. This station has neither beginning nor end; for firstness and lastness pertain to the contingent world and not to the world of God.

order.why: Explore Christ’s spiritual origin.
shortened: Christ is the focal centre of the Holy Spirit; He is born of the Holy Spirit; He has been raised up by the Holy Spirit; He descends from the Holy Spirit--that is, His Reality does not proceed from the lineage of Adam but is born of the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Retain the scriptural reference to Jesus strengthened by the Spirit. End with the joy conveyed through the language of overflowing grace.
shortened: Great God! When the stream of utterance reached this stage, We beheld, and lo! the sweet savors of God were being wafted from the dayspring of Revelation, and the morning breeze was blowing out of the Sheba of the Eternal. Its tidings rejoiced anew the heart, and imparted immeasurable gladness to the soul.
And to Jesus, Son of Mary, We gave manifest signs, and We strengthened Him with the Holy Spirit."

order.why: Keep the parallel reported expression with its source status.
shortened: The Christ is the central point of the Holy Spirit; he was born of the Holy Spirit; he was raised up of the Holy Spirit...

order.why: Turn from origin to the teaching of spiritual virtues.
shortened: The Holy Spirit it is which, through the mediation of the Prophets of God, teaches spiritual virtues to man and enables him to attain Eternal Life.

order.why: Close the linked readings with receiving the Spirit through its teachings.
Return to the vision of the Maiden amid tribulation.
Attend to the address to the Maid of Heaven. Consider the image’s relation to grace throughout creation.
Retain the Báb’s use of the heavenly Maiden image.
shortened: O people of earth! By the True God, I am indeed a Maiden of Paradise whom Glory hath birthed in a palace of moist and moving ruby. By God, I have seen nothing in that Most Great Paradise but that it spoke of the Remembrance in praise of this Arabian Youth.
When He uttereth the Greatest Name, Paradise trembleth with longing for His presence, and when He glorifieth God, Paradise becometh still as snow upon the summit of a frozen mountain.

order.why: Compare the new Jerusalem portrayed as a heavenly maiden.
Include the lament expressed through the same symbolic world.
Revisit the impulse to break silence.
Study the mirror analogy and its rejection of division in the divine Essence.
shortened: The purport of our words is that the reality of Christ was a clear mirror wherein the Sun of Truth--that is, the divine Essence--appeared and shone forth with infinite perfections and attributes. It is not that the Sun, which is the Essence of the Divinity, was ever divided or multiplied, for it remains one, but it became manifest in the mirror. That is why Christ said, "The Father is in the Son," meaning that that Sun is manifest and visible in this mirror.

order.why: Distinguish the fullness attributed to the Prophets from the rays received by others.
shortened: The Holy Spirit is given only to the Prophets; the people can only possess the rays of the Holy Spirit. Those who believe in God have four qualities - growth, sense, intellect, and spiritual or divine life.

order.why: Distinguishes degrees of divine revelation and identifies the Prophets as its recipients.
Read the historical comparison of several religious symbols.
Read the awakening and summons to proclaim.
Connect the Spirit’s aid with the proclamation of commandments.
Retain the Gospel image of heaven opened.
Read the further explanation of sun, rays, and mirror.
Consider heavenly teaching entering human life.
Join the unity of the Spirit with the distinction between eternal and created.

questions: What do images such as a torrent, wind, or light communicate that an abstract definition of revelation might leave out?
How do the sun and mirror analogies help distinguish the divine source, the Holy Spirit, and the Manifestation?
What can be compared between Mark’s account of the dove and the visions described here, and what should remain distinct?
How does the acquisition of spiritual virtues bear upon the meaning of receiving the Spirit?
What might change in our reading when attention moves from the beauty of a symbol to the response it asks of us?

neighbors.invitation: Explore the lamp’s oil, wick, and radiance as images of knowledge, attraction, and love.
Consider how acting upon guidance can deepen knowledge of its source.

references.label: 1 · Mark 1:9–11 · The Spirit descending like a dove
references.note: At Jesus’ baptism, Mark describes opened heavens, the Spirit descending like a dove, and a heavenly voice. Compare the scene’s imagery and proclamation with the collection’s descriptions of revelation, while preserving the distinct theological claims of each source.

subjects.displayTitle: Qur’anic imagery: thirst, renewal, and recognition
subjects.introduction: The thirsty traveller races across the desert toward what looks like water and arrives at nothing. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá borrows that Qur’ánic mirage for the world itself, and for every soul chasing a satisfaction that cannot satisfy. The Qur’án’s own verse runs on from the empty mirage to the reckoning that waits there [1], and reading it whole shows what a later use chooses to stress. Against the mirage stand the images of real sustenance: the sweet Euphrates, the river that is mother of all seas, the barren earth that stirs and swells when rain falls on it, the she-camel of God whose milk quickens souls and bodies. Then come the harder figures, the hamstrung camel and the shattered Ark, Joseph’s bloodied shirt beside the weeping for Ḥusayn, the trumpet and the convulsed heavens, and at the last Moses asked what is in his right hand, his staff read as a bestowed power for tending God’s sheep. A single image can be explicit commentary in one place and prayer or poetry in another. The road continues into the Day of Resurrection and Judgement, and into the wider interpretation of the Qur’án and Ḥadíth.
subjects.arc: Enter through thirst and the mirage, discover images of nourishment and renewal, then read judgment and prophetic memory as calls to recognition and service.

order.why: Begin with the arresting image of thirst pursuing a mirage.
shortened: O spiritual friends of the Great One! In the mighty Qur'an, this world has been likened to a desert mirage, and human souls to one who thirsts for water. The parched person imagines the mirage to be water and races with utmost speed across the desert, only to end up disappointed and at a loss, perishing from thirst.

order.why: Read the quoted Qur’anic verse beside its application.
shortened: This is why God in the Qur'an has likened the strivings, gains and deeds of the heedless to a mirage, saying: "But the deeds of those who disbelieve are like a mirage in a desert. The thirsty one thinks it to be water; until when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing."

order.why: Turn from false water toward the sea and sweet river.
Consider water as wisdom and the foundation of belief.
shortened: Thus have We established for thee, through the waters of Our wisdom and utterance, the foundations of thy belief. This, verily, is the water whereon the Throne of thy Lord hath been raised. "His Throne had stood upon the waters."

order.why: Introduce the river from which other waters flow.
Read the reported interpretation of the four rivers.
Consider the cup of spiritual refreshment.
shortened: O thou who art turned unto God! From the outpourings of the Day of Resurrection thou hast drunk of the pure water, and hast become the manifestation of "The righteous shall drink of a cup tempered with camphor."

order.why: Move from thirst to the earth renewed by rain.
Read the ocean as an image of the Cause in calm and tempest.
shortened: The Baha'i Cause is like unto the Great Ocean or rather the Great Ocean is a sign of the Cause of God. Its mountainous waves are in itself and by itself. While it is in the utmost of calmness, the Northern and Southern winds lash it into furious tempest.

order.why: Introduce the she-camel as a source of nourishment.
Study the interpretation of injury to the she-camel.
Retain the joined imagery of the shattered Ark and hamstrung camel.
shortened: By My life, O thou who hast fixed thy gaze upon My Countenance! The Ark hath been shattered, and the She-Camel hath been hamstrung by reason of that which the hands of the oppressors have wrought.

order.why: Hear the further lament in the same imagery.
shortened: By God! The Cry hath been raised, and the She-Camel hath been hamstrung through that which the hands of them that disbelieved in God, the Lord of Lords, have wrought.

order.why: Read Joseph’s bloodied shirt beside the remembrance of Husayn. Read the further Joseph passage and the joined scriptural allusions.
shortened: "And they brought his shirt with false blood upon it. He said: Nay, but your souls have made a matter light for you, so comely patience! And Allah is He Whose help is sought against what you describe."

O servants of the All-Merciful! God hath prescribed for you, at the mention of Husayn, weeping like unto the weeping of the bereaved, and verily God's judgment concerning vengeance for him hath been decreed in truth.

order.why: Retain the brief conjunction of Kufih and Karbila.
Hear the trumpet as a summons to reflect.
shortened: Reflect now upon that which the All-Merciful hath revealed in the Qur'an, where He clearly saith: "And there shall be a blast on the trumpet, and all who are in the heavens and all who are in the earth shall swoon away, save those whom God shall please to exempt. Then shall there be another blast on it, and lo! they shall rise and gaze around them.

order.why: Read the cluster of images concerning the Day.
shortened: This is that day of which He saith: "And thou shalt see mankind as drunken, yet they are not drunken: but severe is the chastisement of God."

And this is that Day of which He saith: "The trumpet shall be blown, and all who are in the heavens and on earth shall swoon away, save him whom God pleaseth." And likewise He saith: "All things shall perish save His face."

order.why: Consider cosmic upheaval as a proclamation of resurrection.
Retain the cited expectation of the Lord’s coming.
shortened: Hearken unto that which the All-Merciful hath sent down in the Qur'an: "On the day when thy Lord shall come, or some of the signs of thy Lord shall come."

order.why: Consider the challenge that revelation can pose to accepted learning.
Ask how a word of acceptance changes the significance of material objects.
Read sacred lineage and sacred places as expressions of devotion.
shortened: O descendant of His Holiness Khalil the All-Merciful! Truly you are of the noble lineage of His Holiness Khalil and progeny of that sacred and cherished being, for you hastened to the shade of the tent of martyrdom, and entered the temple of the Lord in the Furthest Mosque, and in the Holy of Holies became occupied with chanting the verses of unity.

order.why: Retain the cry of longing through sacred geography.
Turn the same geography into prayer for good.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Him through the light of Whose countenance the heavens were illumined and through the fragrance of Whose raiment Yathrib and Batha were perfumed, to ordain for me all the good Thou hast ordained in Thy Book for Thy loved ones.

order.why: Consider the remembered gesture toward Salman and the search for knowledge.
Read Abraham’s desire for a heart at rest.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy Greatest Name to cast tranquility into the heart of Thy servant Hatam Muhammad, that his heart may find peace in Thy irrevocable Cause, for Thou hast placed the station of peace above faith, as Thou hast made clear in Thy Holy Book and Thy Mighty Qur'an, addressing Abraham: "Dost thou not believe?" He said: "Yes, but that my heart may be at rest." Thus didst Thou confirm his certain knowledge with the vision of certainty and the truth of certainty.

order.why: Attend to forgiveness and repentance.
shortened: O Lord of pardon and forgiveness, Concealer of faults and Swift to bestow favors! Thou hast praised Thyself in the clear verses of the Qur'an as "Accepter of repentance, Forgiver of sins," and "Verily God forgives all sins."

order.why: Include the prayer for refuge from envy and darkness.
shortened: Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the Dawn, from the evil of what He has created, and from the evil of darkness when it overspreads, and from the evil of those who blow on knots, and from the evil of the envious one when he envieth.

order.why: Turn the image of captivity toward spiritual flight.
Invite the reader to become a lamp and an ornament of the garden.
Close the linked readings with prophetic qualities gathered into a prayer for service.
shortened: Bestow abundantly the Holy Spirit's grace and freely grant the power of the Faithful Spirit, so that Your loved ones may arise to serve You with celestial might, heavenly power, divine sovereignty, heavenly confirmation, celestial hosts, a merciful breath, divine bounty, the white hand of Moses, the breath of Christ, the friendship of Abraham, the love of Muhammad, the beauty of Joseph, the longing of Jacob, and the patience of Job.

order.why: End with the interpretation of Moses’ staff as a bestowed power.
Explains the relation of the letter Ba, Bismillah and the Opening Surah to the Quran as a whole.

questions: What kinds of desire or achievement might resemble the mirage described in these readings?
How does reading the full Qur’anic mirage verse affect our understanding of its later applications?
What different relationships to spiritual life are suggested by water, a lamp, a garden, and a staff?
How can we distinguish an explicit interpretation from a poetic allusion or a prayer that reuses an image?
What would it mean to carry a scriptural image into action, becoming a source of illumination or nourishment for others?

neighbors.invitation: Study the niche, glass, and lamp as a coordinated image of illumination.
Consider an ark upon the ocean as language for deliverance and steadfastness.

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 24:39 · The mirage and the reckoning
references.note: The verse compares unbelievers’ deeds to a mirage pursued by someone thirsty, then turns from the failed expectation of water to an encounter with divine reckoning. Compare the full verse with the selections that apply the mirage to worldly striving and heedlessness.

subjects.displayTitle: Satan and the insistent self: vigilance without enmity
subjects.introduction: Asked what Satan is, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answered in three words: the insistent self. The Bahá’í writings turn the old warning inward. There is no personal devil and no satanic tree; humanity grows on one tree of divine mercy, and the enemy is the ego that wants to win every hour, the pride that made a glorious angel fall when he looked at the niche and missed the lamp, the self-righteousness that was the Pharisee’s devil while the tax-collector’s confessed sins became his angel. Whatever makes you heedless of God, for that time, is your Satan. Vigilance is therefore needed against deception in its subtler dress, refinement hiding base intent, humility that is only a pose, error spoken in the name of truth. James tracing temptation to a person’s own desire makes a close companion [1], without closing every Christian question about the devil. The task is to examine the motives behind one’s conduct while refusing to sort people into sacred and demonic kinds, and to stay steadfast without quarrelling. From here the way leads to selfishness and egotism, to the nonexistence of evil, and to heaven and hell.
subjects.arc: Begin with the insistent self and the unity of humanity, examine pride and deceptive appearances, and conclude with steadfastness and freedom from contention.

order.why: Open with the concise identification of Satan as the insistent self.
Uses Satan as the first self-conceited one in an exhortation to humility.
Immediately place vigilance within the one tree of humanity.
shortened: He says, "Ye are all the leaves of one tree." He does not say, "Ye are the leaves of two trees: one divine, the other satanic." He has declared that each individual member of the human family is a leaf or branch upon the Adamic tree; that all are sheltered beneath the protecting mercy and providence of God; that all are the children of God, fruit upon the one tree of His love. God is equally compassionate and kind to all the leaves, branches and fruit of this tree. Therefore, there is no satanic tree whatever -- Satan being a product of human minds and of instinctive human tendencies toward error.

order.why: Explore several meanings and the danger of self-righteousness.
shortened: Again, there is a devil within man, just as there is the divine voice within man. Anything, for the time that makes you become heedless of God is your Satan.

In the story of the Pharisees and the tax-gatherer praying in the Temple, the self-righteousness of the Pharisee was his devil, whereas the sins and the shortcomings of the Tax-gatherer which drew him toward God, to confess, and entreat pardon for them became his angel. The word of satan or devil means the opponent of God, - there is no entity of that name.

order.why: Retain the explicit denial of a personal devil.
Consider the ego’s recurring pressure.
Distinguish outward refinement from inward intention.
Name the destructive actions associated with the call of Satan.
shortened: The call of Satan is: "Hasten to falsehood! Hasten to calumny! Hasten to the pursuit of self and passion! Hasten to love of the world! Hasten to tyranny! Hasten to disobedience! Hasten to pride and arrogance! Hasten to evil conduct and manners!"

order.why: Focus on vanity.
shortened: The first person that was vain and pleased with himself was the Satan. Vanity is one of the characteristics of Satan.

order.why: Read the reported fall through preoccupation with self.
shortened: Sacred history records that Satan was favored at the Threshold of God and was the teacher of the angels, and in every one of the seven heavens he was known by a holy name. As soon as he began to see himself, to think of himself he was fallen.

order.why: Study the fuller account of pride that mistakes the shell for the pearl.
shortened: Though he was among the greatest angels of heaven, he descended to the lowest plane when he grew proud and said "I am the most noble, the most high," veiled by elements from the dazzling Light. He looked at the physical temple and earthly element while heedless of the divine mystery deposited in that luminous temple. He focused on the niche while neglecting the lamp, and saw the dark shells while ignorant of the radiant and noble Pearl hidden in that supreme shell.

order.why: Compare worldly dominion with the light of truth.
shortened: The whole globe is nothing before one ray of the Sun of Truth.

Thus it is said in the Gospel that Satan took Christ to the top of a high mountain, showed Him the world outspread and told Him that he would give Him all these things if he would follow him. But Christ refused.

order.why: Read the summons to belief and refuge from whispering.
shortened: O people of the earth! Believe in the Light which God has sent down with Me in pure truth, and follow not the footsteps of Satan, for he commands you to associate partners with God, your Lord.
O Remembrance of God! Say: Seek refuge with God from the evil of the whisperer who whispers in people's breasts, for verily your Lord, God the Truth, is ever watchful over all things.

order.why: Acknowledge human weakness and susceptibility to doubt.
Consider the loss associated with deceptive promptings.
shortened: Some, through the whisperings of the Evil One, were deprived of the ocean of Thy mercy, while others were illumined by the effulgences of the Sun of Truth.

order.why: Read the particular account of deception before revelation.
shortened: Observe thou the first one who denied God - he stood before the Face while We sent down verses unto him, until Satan deceived him, who was indeed mankind's manifest enemy.

order.why: Examine the confidence of those who suppose themselves rightly guided.
shortened: They have forsaken the Self-Subsisting and clung to vain imaginings, having followed the promptings of the Evil Ones who turn people away from this Most Great Ocean while supposing themselves to be guided aright.

order.why: Attend to deception in the name of truth.
Consider the desire for an enduring name.
shortened: O Pen of Command! Make mention in the Tablet of that which Satan uttered in those days when he said unto his hosts: "Come ye and help me, that your names may endure upon the earth." Thus did he whisper into the breasts of the idolaters.

order.why: Read the warning about varied appearances.
Retain the extension of that warning to every city.
Consider the broad reach attributed to misleading influences.
Read the interruption of access to divine fragrances.
shortened: We have not forgotten thee, but Satan hath lurked in every pathway, and thus the divine fragrances have been withheld from God's successful servants.

order.why: Turn the warning into an invitation to deliverance through light.
Seek steadfastness rather than confidence in oneself.
shortened: Seek steadfastness from God, for verily the satans lie in ambush for the servants with utmost craftiness and ever have done so.

order.why: Connect preservation of a station with effort.
shortened: Exert your utmost effort and striving to preserve this lofty and most exalted station, for the satans lie in ambush and the Cause is in God's hands, the True Sovereign, the Manifest.

order.why: Return to firmness amid vain imaginings.
shortened: Stand firm in that whereunto thou hast attained, for verily Satan lieth in wait and calleth the people unto vain imaginings.

order.why: Give remembrance and refuge a daily rhythm.
shortened: Remember your Lord at eventide and at dawn, and guard yourselves against the wiles of Satan, for he appeareth at all times with cunning. Seek ye refuge in God, O company of the righteous, that He may, through His power and sovereignty, protect you from his evil.

order.why: Consider steadfast attachment to the Beloved.
Close the linked readings with active service despite whisperings.
Retain the further warning about false appearances of humility.
Read prayer as an inward struggle against pride.
shortened: O you who are firm in the Covenant! You had asked for the interpretation of your dream.

And afterward, standing in the prayer niche indicates resistance against the people of contention and the opponents of the Covenant of the Lord of Majesty, for the prayer niche is the place of battle with Satan, and through worship of the All-Merciful in the prayer niche, man wages war with "the first one who refused and showed pride."

order.why: End with the refusal to quarrel, even with an opponent.

questions: How does interpreting Satan as the insistent self change the practical meaning of spiritual vigilance?
Why might self-righteousness or apparent humility become harder to recognize than an openly destructive impulse?
What does James’ account of desire contribute to the discussion, and what questions does it leave open?
How can we assess harmful conduct without dividing humanity into inherently divine and inherently satanic groups?
What practices might help us resist pride and deception while remaining free from quarrelling and contempt?

neighbors.invitation: Read the request for protection from idle fancy alongside the request for knowledge.
Compare inward interpretations of the garden’s figures without turning symbolic roles into fixed judgments of people.

references.label: 1 · James 1:13–18 · Desire and temptation
references.note: James traces temptation through a person’s own desire and distinguishes this process from the good gifts attributed to God. Compare that inward attention with the compilation’s treatment of ego and destructive qualities. This passage does not by itself define every Christian view of Satan.

subjects.displayTitle: Colour and light: learning to see through symbols
subjects.introduction: Light is the manifestor of all things, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes to a handmaiden; without it everything would stay hidden behind the veil of darkness. The imagery of light then asks what makes meaning visible. A lamp shining through glass lights up a room; a black stone facing the sun shows nothing, while a clean mirror returns the sun with all its perfections; a crystal catches fire when it is turned toward the light. The Qur’an’s parable of the niche, the lamp, the glass and the oil from a blessed tree is read here as knowledge, attraction, love and the illumined face, light upon light [1]. Colour belongs to the same grammar, but with more than one vocabulary: in the Báb’s writings white, yellow, green and crimson mark the stages of divine creative action, and the leaves and branches of the Burning Bush speak in those hues, while other reported explanations assign different correspondences, so each must be read in its own setting rather than as a universal code. One statement overrides all of them: God judges hearts and souls, not whiteness or blackness of skin. The journey continues into the soul as a mirror, the divine light and attributes within every person, and the wider play of light and darkness, asking how beauty sharpens perception and how received light can become understanding and peace for others.
subjects.arc: Begin with light’s power to reveal, explore the lamp and mirror, examine differing colour vocabularies, and return to illumination expressed in life.

order.why: Read the complete niche-and-lamp image and its personal application.
Open with light making hidden things manifest.
Give the reader the simple image of light through glass.
shortened: When the light of the lamp shines through glass, its surroundings become illumined.

order.why: Explore the oil, wick, and radiance through knowledge, attraction, and love.
Connect hearing and following with a crystal facing the sun.
Distinguish enduring light from its changing holder.
Consider the different relations of bodies and luminosity.
shortened: O Munir! Luminous bodies are divided into several types. One has a dark and gloomy body but borrows light from another, like the orb of the moon which is dark in itself but acquires light from the sun.

The third type of luminous bodies is pure light itself, where its body is identical with its light and its light identical with its body - essence is identical with existence and existence identical with essence.

order.why: Retain the historical comparison of physical light, sight, and intellect.
Examine the mirror’s receptivity to illumination.
Read light as a station of the Word.
Consider utterance as a lamp within creation.
Read white garments through an interpretation of sanctification.
shortened: The white garments signify holy dignity and a station sanctified from color, i.e., free from the universal conditions and material qualities. That luminous countenance, manifested in beauty, signifieth that the divine lights shone forth from the human form, which were reflected and descended upon thee, dazzling the eyes of those who were perceiving it as the sun dazzles the eyes of those who try to look upon it.

order.why: Make the explicit rejection of colour as a measure of human worth central.
Introduce one reported vocabulary of colour symbolism.
Place a different reported set of correspondences beside it.
Enter the Báb’s interwoven language of colour.
shortened: For it is the embellishment of Glory in the pillar of praise, it is the embellishment of yellow in the pillar of decree, it is the embellishment of beginning in the pillar of green, and it is the embellishment of origination in the pillar of red. If thou sayest red, then it hath adorned the yellow with white, and if thou sayest green, then it hath adorned the white with red. Blessed is it! It is eternally red, imperishably white, perpetually green, and regally yellow.

order.why: Move from symbolic colours to the garment of spring.
shortened: The life-giving spring from that best religion will clothe the world in a garment of rose and hyacinth and jasmine and violet and wild rose and leaf and blossom.

order.why: Consider the effects of divine radiance upon heart and soul.
shortened: In any case, praise be to God that the luminous rays of that divine Orb have fallen upon the crowns of those divine friends, and its heat has influenced the world of heart and soul, making them divine, merciful and illumined.

order.why: Turn illumination into a call to burn with love.
shortened: O thou who art assured by the verses of God! Be thou as a candle among the friends and burn away the veils of the people of possibility with the flame of love for the Beauty of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Connect the image of scriptural rays with peace among peoples.
shortened: Just as the rays of the sun concentrate themselves in a mirror and are reflected, so are the Prophetic Rays of Light of His Holiness Baha'u'llah reflected in the lines of this Book, and their luminous refulgence is shed on the fortunate reader and enlightens his understanding. Let us look at the nine rays of light emanating from the book of Ishraqat:
1.	The oneness of mankind shall be promulgated, in that the Baha'is will endeavour with all their power and capacity (might) to bring about peace among peoples.

order.why: Close the linked readings with a prayer for mercy and light.
Revisit the distinction among visibility, discovery, and perception.
shortened: The mysteries of love are the secrets of the heart, not something perceived by hearing and sight. They are connected and conditioned upon spiritual sensibilities, not upon worldly senses. The light of this universal sun makes things visible - it is the manifester of things, not their discoverer. The light of sight discovers things but does not comprehend them. The light of truth is the manifester of things, the discoverer of things, and the comprehender of things.

order.why: Retain the reported response to colour as experience.
shortened: It is evident that certain colors refresh the heart and promote the elevation of feelings. For instance, the color green brings tranquility and joy to the heart.

order.why: Read the further explanation of a particular symbolic terminology.
shortened: As to Kaf and Za, these are among the isolated letters which were revealed at the opening of one of the blessed Tablets, [BH01494] and the meaning intended is the name Kazim. And by the Crimson Land and the Crimson Hill is meant the station of Decree (qada); for in the terminology of the people of God, the White denoteth the station of the Will, the Green the station of Destiny, the Red the station of Decree, and the Yellow the station of Execution.

order.why: Gives explicit symbolic meanings of white, green, red and yellow and relates crimson to martyrdom.
Consider the provisional translation’s coloured mirrors.

Read the repeated image of differently coloured leaves. Retain the arrangement of colours in heavenly clothing. Attend to the supplied prayer through precious stones. Read chambers, jewels, and praise as a symbolic setting. Preserve the further imagery of jewels and heavenly figures. Read the supplied repetition of light upon light. Widen the imagery of light in every direction. End with praise of the sovereignty over all lights.
shortened: Say: This is a white leaf unto God, the Lord of all worlds. Say: This is a yellow leaf unto God, the Lord of all worlds. Say: This is a green leaf unto God, the Lord of all worlds. Say: This is a red leaf unto God, the Lord of all worlds.

Say: This is a light above every light. Say: This is a light before every light. Say: This is a light after every light. Say: This is a light above all lights. Say: This is a light beneath all lights. Say: This is a light to the right of every light, then to its left, then from every direction that leadeth unto it. God createth every light by His command. Verily, He is the Light in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them.

Grant me stored white diamonds, then hidden yellow gems, then layered green emeralds, then engraved red rubies, lest my soul be saddened among the people by what is given to those who believe in God and His signs.

order.why: Return to the purity of glass and luminosity of the lamp.
Keep the supplied scholarly discussion distinct from the passages it quotes.
shortened: Here the Bab is identified with the various colours of the leaf, the branch, or the tree. These colours express symbolically the synthesis, in the Bab, of the four levels of the covenant. This point becomes clear when we note the symbolic meaning of colours in both the early and later writings of the Bab: in terms of the stages of divine creative Action, white is the colour of the Primal Will; yellow indicates Determination, green represents Destiny, and crimson corresponds to Decree. This colour symbolism enables us to understand why the Bab is simultaneously the Snow-White Tree, the Yellow Leaf, and the Green Branch, as well as the Crimson Leaf of that Tree.

questions: How do a lamp, a mirror, and a shining sun illuminate different relationships between receiving light and sharing it?
What does the Qur’anic parable contribute when read beside the interpretations of oil, wick, glass, and niche?
How should we approach colour correspondences that vary among sources or symbolic vocabularies?
Why is the statement about judging the soul and heart important when reading images of whiteness, blackness, and purity?
What might distinguish being impressed by beautiful imagery from allowing it to change the way we understand and serve others?

neighbors.invitation: Explore the Holy Spirit through rays shining from Christ upon the mirrors of the apostles.
Consider the invitation to become a lamp in the path of God.

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 24:35 · The niche, lamp, and light
references.note: The verse develops a parable through a niche, lamp, glass, and oil from a blessed tree, and explicitly presents this as a likeness connected with divine guidance. Compare its linked images with the compilation’s interpretations, without assuming that all later colour symbolism is contained in the verse.

subjects.displayTitle: Praying through difficulty: honesty, relief, and endurance
subjects.introduction: My tongue is weary of remembrance, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays, because sorrow has scattered my thoughts; and in that admission lies a whole school of prayer. The prayers of Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá for hard times do not pretend. They name loneliness, exile, shut doors, tyrants, debt, the hurt dealt by friends as well as enemies, and they ask outright for the difficulty to be removed. In the same breath they ask for patience, steadfastness and the strength to go on turning toward God, and some of them speak with startling ardor of longing for tribulation in the path of love, a language better received as a lover’s cry than as a demand laid on anyone else’s suffering. Psalm 13 travels a kindred road, from how long to hear me to I will sing [1]. To pray this way is to keep an honest relationship with God in the dark, and to notice the burdens of others more sharply. The way continues into tests and trials themselves, into sacrifice and suffering, and into the wider world of prayer.
subjects.arc: Begin with unguarded distress, ask for relief and protection, explore endurance and devotion, and end with care for the concrete burdens of others.

order.why: Bring gathered tribulation into a plea for nearness and forgiveness.
shortened: O God, my God! Be Thou not far from me, for tribulation upon tribulation hath gathered about me.
Beneath the ocean of Thy forgiveness, faced with the restlessness of the leviathan of glory, immerse me, for my sins have utterly doomed me.

order.why: Open with sorrow that makes remembrance itself difficult.
shortened: O Lord! Have mercy upon my solitude and my anguish, comfort me in my loneliness, and show compassion to me in my estrangement and distress. O Lord! My tongue is weary of remembrance due to the intensity of my sorrows, and my understanding falls short due to my scattered thoughts. I have no refuge to which I might repair, nor any shelter wherein I might take protection. O Lord! Fulfill what Thou hast promised me and bring to pass that wherewith Thou hast assured me, for I am at my wit's end with my tribulation, and my anguish and affliction have intensified.

order.why: Hear the plea when hope seems closed.
Name solitude, separation, and hardship.
shortened: Save me from the depths of the seas of tribulation, deliver me from the pit of hardship and adversity, comfort me in the terror of solitude and the supreme ordeal, and rescue me from the shock of deprivation and the burning anguish of separation and exile.

order.why: Ask for the doors of hope to be opened.
shortened: The doors of hope have been shut against the hearts that long for Thee, O my Lord! Their keys are in Thy hands; open them by the power of Thy might and Thy sovereignty.

order.why: Offer a brief prayer for difficulties to be removed.
Widen deliverance to anguish, sorrow, and bondage.
Pray for sorrow to become joy and hardship ease.
Bring the pangs of a people into the request for comfort.
shortened: Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by this Name, which hath been encompassed by tribulations from all directions and upon which calamities have descended from every quarter, to such extent that it findeth no helper in Thy earth nor any succorer in Thy dominion, that Thou mayest ease for this people the pangs of travail, preserve them therefrom, deliver them from this hardship, and transform it into comfort and tranquility.

order.why: Pray for changes in material as well as inward conditions.
Ask for protection from tyranny.
shortened: I beseech Thee to preserve me from the tyrannous ones among Thy servants who have turned away from Thy beauty and denied Thy signs.

order.why: Retain the direct plea for release from another’s clutches.
Extend protection to the whole company of loved ones.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the lights of Thy Most Great Name and the mysteries hidden in Thy knowledge, O Lord of eternity, to deliver Thy loved ones from the evil of every oppressor. Then preserve them, O my God, through Thy grace and Thy hosts and Thy sovereignty, and ordain for them that which will draw them nigh unto Thee.

order.why: Name the hurt caused by enemies and friends alike.
shortened: Aid me through Your grace and bounty from the Supreme Concourse and raise me to the Most Exalted Horizon, that I may find rest from the assaults of enemies and the stones cast by the criticism of the loved ones.

order.why: Ask for deliverance from harmful suggestions.
shortened: O Lord, deliver us from all temptations, tests and evil suggestions of those who turned their faces from Thee.

order.why: Join protection from imagination with the gift of knowledge.
shortened: Keep safe Thy servants and Thy handmaidens, O my Lord, from the darts of idle fancy and vain imaginings, and give them from the hands of Thy grace a draught of the soft-flowing waters of Thy knowledge.

order.why: Bring deliverance, purification, and steadfastness together.
shortened: Therefore, O my God, I beseech Thee by Thy Name through which the Ark of Thy Cause did sail upon the ocean of Thy will, that Thou mayest deliver me from my condition, purify my heart through Thy knowledge, and make me steadfast in Thy Cause and Thy love.

order.why: Read the sequence of worship, assistance, and guidance.
Hold patience in separation together with a request for relief.
shortened: Be patient in separation from meeting your Lord, then beseech God to remove our anguish and bring us relief. Verily there is no God but Him.

order.why: Consider supplication as a way to seek patience.
shortened: Verily, in both cases we must supplicate and implore and commune to the divine Threshold in order to be patient in ordeals.

order.why: Read the full prayer for contentment and confidence amid ordeal.
Ask that tribulation not prevent turning toward God.
Enter the devotional image of tests as healing medicine.
shortened: O Thou Whose tests are a healing medicine to such as are nigh unto Thee, Whose sword is the ardent desire of all them that love Thee, Whose dart is the dearest wish of those hearts that yearn after Thee, Whose decree is the sole hope of them that have recognized Thy truth!

order.why: Read gratitude for strength to bear the Cause.
Provides words of prayer for divine aid, strength and ability under otherwise unbearable trials.
Attend carefully to the intense language of longing for suffering in love.
Keep that devotion joined to the plea for ease and capacity to serve.
shortened: O my God, my God! Your love has set me ablaze, and my remoteness from the shore of Your nearness has consumed me, causing my veins to be severed and my liver to melt. I beseech You by Your Prophets and Your chosen ones, by the mysteries of Your Kingdom and Your Dominion, and by the Mother Book which none has known save You, to aid me in that which You love and are pleased with, and to assist me in serving Your chosen ones and Your loved ones. Then grant me the best of what You have revealed in Your Book. O Lord! You see that hardship has encompassed me and difficulty has seized me. Where is Your ease, O Master of existence, and Your repose, O Sovereign of the seen and unseen?

order.why: Retain the striking reported cry of humiliation.
Return to the sorrow shared with an afflicted person and family.
shortened: My God, my God! Thou seest me standing at Thy sacred threshold, supplicating Thee and humbled before Thy door. I call upon Thee with my spirit and my heart, and commune with Thee with my soul and my tongue, saying: My God, my God! Verily Thy servant Husayn hath fallen into an affliction at which the peoples of both East and West are dismayed, and hath been tried with a trial that bringeth sorrow to his parents, nay, that grieveth the hearts of all who love him, even from the farthest lands of East and West, causing tears to flow from every eye.

order.why: Pray for consolation and joy for those who have suffered.
shortened: Write down, then, for such as have been afflicted with adversities for Thy sake, the reward of those who have suffered martyrdom in the path of Thy good-pleasure. Send down, moreover, upon them, O Lord, that which will rejoice their hearts, solace their eyes, and exhilarate their souls.

order.why: Ask for hearts to be gladdened after sorrow.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O my God, by the light of Thy countenance whereby earth and heaven were illumined, to send down from the heaven of Thy grace that which shall gladden the hearts of Thy loved ones after this sorrow which hath clouded the pure wine of assurance in Thy days.

order.why: Close the linked readings with the hope of release into spaciousness.
shortened: From the pit thou shalt rise to the summit of glory and from the narrow confines of this incarceration thou shalt ascend to soul-entrancing gardens and meadows.

order.why: Retain the request for inward purification.
shortened: Thou dost witness what Thou dost witness, how particles of evil and intimations of doubt have encompassed me, such that they have prevented me from entering the city of Thy reunion and soaring in the atmosphere of the glory of meeting with Thee. I beseech Thee therefore, O my Beloved, by Him Whom Thou hast made the Ruler over all contingent beings and the Sovereign over all who dwell in the earth and the heavens, that Thou mayest purify my heart from the whisperings of Satan, O Thou in Whose hand is the dominion of might and certitude.

order.why: End with protection connected to a concrete financial burden.

questions: What room do these prayers make for honesty when sorrow weakens our ability to feel hopeful or even to pray?
How can requests for relief and requests for endurance belong within the same relationship with God?
What does Psalm 13’s movement from lament toward trust add to our reading?
How might we approach the intense language of longing for tribulation without imposing it on someone else’s suffering?
How could praying for others deepen practical attention to their loneliness, oppression, or material burdens?

neighbors.invitation: Consider how humility about one’s own shortcomings may become a movement toward God.
Read the image of barren ground receiving life-giving rain.

references.label: 1 · Psalm 13 · Lament, petition, and trust
references.note: The psalm begins by asking how long abandonment and sorrow will continue, petitions God to hear, and turns toward trust and praise. Compare these movements with the collection’s different voices of distress and confidence, without treating them as a timetable every person must follow.

subjects.displayTitle: Recognition and action: faith becoming a way of life
subjects.introduction: The short prayer a Bahá’í says each noon begins by confessing why a human being exists at all: to know God and to worship Him. Those two verbs set the shape of a whole life. Bahá’u’lláh names recognition of the Manifestation of God as the first duty laid upon His servants, and observance of His ordinances as the second, and declares the twin duties inseparable, neither acceptable without the other. The claim is strong, and it comes with careful distinctions: a good deed done without recognition is still praiseworthy, though it is a beautiful body without a spirit; intention gives an action its spiritual character; and divine mercy can never be reduced to a tally of achievement. Jesus asked why people called Him Lord and did not do what He said, and compared hearing with doing to a house built on rock [1]; ‘Abdu’l-Bahá presses the same point when He says that in this day faith consists not in belief but in deeds, and that a Bahá’í must justify the name by a life. Obedience here is a free response, not a yoke. The journey leads into the recognition of God, the laws of the Kitáb-i-Aqdas, and the meaning of servitude and submission.
subjects.arc: Begin with human purpose, establish the inseparability of recognition and action, clarify motives and distinctions, and end with free response and hope in mercy.

order.why: Open with the brief statement of being created to know and worship.
shortened: I bear witness, O my God, that Thou hast created me to know Thee and to worship Thee.

order.why: Consider the capacity both to know and to reflect divine glory.
Join worship to recognition.
shortened: The beginning of all utterance is the worship of God, and this followeth upon His recognition.

order.why: Read the foundational statement of the twin duties. Revisit the twin duties with the supplied explanatory note.
Immediately retain the distinction between good and harmful deeds among those without recognition.
shortened: This verse does not mean that those who are veiled from God are all equal whether they be doers of good or workers of iniquity. It means only that the foundation is the recognition of God and that good deeds derive from this knowledge. Nevertheless, it is certain that among those who are veiled from God there is a difference between the doer of good and the sinner and malefactor.

This blessed verse means therefore that good deeds alone, without the recognition of God, cannot lead to eternal redemption, to everlasting success and salvation, and to admittance into the Kingdom of God.

order.why: Explore the roles of knowledge, love, and sincere intention. Develop the relation of knowledge, love, intention, and action.
shortened: Briefly, good deeds become perfect and complete only after the knowledge of God has been acquired, the love of God has been manifested, and spiritual attractions and goodly motives have been attained.  Otherwise, though good deeds be praiseworthy, if they do not spring from the knowledge of God, from the love of God, and from a sincere intention, they will be imperfect.

order.why: Consider the reciprocal dependence of recognition and action.
Give the relation a concise expression.
shortened: Say: Deeds must follow recognition - thus have you been commanded in all the Tablets and in this blessed, mighty and praiseworthy Tablet.

order.why: Hear the personal invitation to follow recognition with practice.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! Your call was heard and you have attained the Most Great Bounty which is the recognition of the Lord of Eternity. Now strive to act according to His ordinances which have been sent down from the Holy Pen in the Most Holy Book.

order.why: Revisit recognition as a first step.
shortened: The first step is the recognition of God, exalted be His glory, and afterward to act according to that which hath been sent down in the Book from the Pen of the All-Bountiful.

order.why: Read adherence as the continuing counterpart of recognition.
shortened: Two most great matters have been and shall ever be: first, the recognition of the Ancient Being, and second, adherence to that which hath dawned from the horizon of His Command.

order.why: Focus on constancy in the Cause.
shortened: I summon the loved ones of God, exalted be His glory, to two most great matters: first, the recognition of the Ancient Being, and second, steadfastness in His Cause.

order.why: Join gratitude for recognition with steadfastness.
shortened: Give thanks to thy Lord for having aided thee to recognize the Dawning-Place of Revelation and for having made thee among those who have turned unto Him. The first duty is the recognition of God, exalted be His glory, and after this steadfastness in this mighty Cause.

order.why: Explicitly connects recognition with steadfastness and observance of revealed ordinances.
Consider faith, certainty, and conduct together.
shortened: The cause of eternal glory to man is faith and certainty and then living (or acting) according to the behests of His Majesty the Eternal God. My hope is that thou wilt attain to the three.

order.why: Ask how learning bears fruit in responsiveness. Retain the supplied interpretation of Paradise. Ask how recognition of a new revelation changes inherited practices.
shortened: How vast the number of people who are well versed in every science, yet it is their adherence to the holy Word of God which will determine their faith, inasmuch as the fruit of every science is none other than the knowledge of divine precepts and submission unto His good-pleasure.
All the letters of the sublime paradise of the Bayan return unto Him Whom God shall make manifest, Who is the First Gate of the paradise, and the Most Great Name Who is manifest by divinity.

Do ye attend most carefully to this matter, and take heed (for it is inevitable that ye shall meet Him) lest ye show this degree of deference – and perform your works – for His name, while for the Bearer of this name ye do not what ye were performing for His mere appellation (albeit, did ye know it to be Him, ye would perform your works for Him; yet ye confuse the matter in your own eyes).

order.why: Retain the Báb’s summons to obedience.
shortened: God desireth naught from you on this day save obedience to God's true Command through the truth -- an everlasting reward from God, the Ancient One.

order.why: Read the relation of piety, deeds, and character.
Consider recognition in relation to creation’s purpose.
shortened: God hath created all specifically for the recognition of the Dawning-Place of His verses and the Dayspring of His evidences.

order.why: Close the linked readings with the claim concerning the revelation’s relation to earlier Books.
shortened: All the Books have been sent down in order to establish the truth of this Cause. Whoso turneth away hath verily denied God and His Messengers and His Books which were sent unto the worlds. Say: All Books have been expounded from this mighty Book. He who denieth this Book, naught shall be accepted from him though he act according to what is in the Books of God, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. All things have been made dependent upon this Cause - this if ye be of them that comprehend. Every mention hath been consummated by this Mention and every foundation by this firm Foundation.

order.why: Consider steadfastness as the end toward which faith moves.
Consider the pairing of conduct and faith through Paul and Peter.
shortened: We must strive to awaken sleeping souls, make the heedless mindful, and bring the divine teachings, which are the spirit of this age, to the ears of the people of the world. They must be published in newspapers and eloquently explained in gatherings. The approach should be like Paul's and the faith like Peter's.

order.why: Turn profession into efforts to improve the condition of all.
shortened: Faith does not consist in belief, it consists in deeds. It is not sufficient to believe in Baha'u'llah and to say, "I am of the people of El-Abha"; we must act in accordance with the teachings of Baha'u'llah, who commands us to become centers of divine attraction, so that the attributes of God may emanate from us, that we may become wise and well intentioned to all the peoples of the earth in order to better the condition of all.

order.why: Read the fuller challenge to justify a name by a life.
shortened: They should justify their claim to be Baha'is by deeds and not by name. He is a true Baha'i who strives by day and by night to progress and advance along the path of human endeavour, whose most cherished desire is so to live and act as to enrich and illuminate the world, whose source of inspiration is the essence of divine virtue, whose aim in life is so to conduct himself as to be the cause of infinite progress. Only when he attains unto such perfect gifts can it be said of him that he is a true Baha'i. For in this holy Dispensation, the crowning glory of bygone ages and cycles, true faith is no mere acknowledgement of the unity of God, but rather the living of a life that will manifest all the perfections and virtues implied in such belief.

order.why: Distinguish steadfast love and observance within that response.
Return to knowledge and worship through the longer prayer of dependence.
Read beginning and end through knowledge and observance.
Read the priority assigned to steadfastness after recognition.
Read faith through conscious knowledge and good deeds.
Consider the twin duties as an exercise of free will.
Retain the parallel statement of freely chosen response.
End with a noble life, regard for others, and hope in divine mercy.

questions: How might acting upon a teaching deepen our understanding of it rather than merely demonstrate what we already know?
What different roles do knowledge, love, intention, and steadfastness play in a life of faith?
How does Luke’s image of a foundation help us examine the distance between religious language and practice?
Why do the distinctions concerning praiseworthy deeds and divine mercy matter when reading the strong claims about recognition?
What would it mean to understand obedience as a freely chosen response, and how might that response become visible in the way we treat others?

neighbors.invitation: Consider receiving spiritual bounty through embracing heavenly teachings.
Explore steadfast response when tribulation makes the path difficult.

references.label: 1 · Luke 6:46–49 · Hearing, doing, and building
references.note: Jesus challenges an address of loyalty that is not accompanied by action, then compares hearing and doing with a house founded on rock. Read this beside the compilation’s account of recognition and practice, attending also to its distinct teaching about successive Manifestations.
